'''Lars Sverker Johansson''' is a Swedish [[physicist]], [[linguist]], textbook author and university professor. He created [[Lsjbot]], a [[Wikipedia bots|Wikipedia bot]].

== Biography ==
Sverker Johansson is a [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctor of philosophy]] in [[physics]] and a [[Master of Philosophy|master of philosophy]] in [[linguistics]]. He received his doctorate in physics in 1990 on a thesis in [[particle physics]] on μμ and eμ pair production at the experiment HELIOS at the collider SPS and software development for the experiment DELPHI at the collider LEP, both experiments at CERN. He has subsequently worked as a researcher in several fields, mainly neutrino-related particle physics with the AMANDA experiment but also in the origin of language.

During his career, he has mainly worked at the University of Jönköping.

Johansson's book ''Origins of Language, Constraints of Hypotheses, and Convergence Evidence in Language and Communication Studies'', published in 2005, has been reviewed by the ''Journal of Linguistics''.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 October 2014|title=ICLA Review of Sverker Johansson (2005), Origins of Language|url=http://www.cogling.org/Reviews/johansson.shtml|access-date=4 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013173933/http://www.cogling.org/Reviews/johansson.shtml|archive-date=13 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=13 October 2014|title=Hypothetically Speaking » American Scientist|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/hypothetically-speaking|access-date=4 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013222046/http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/hypothetically-speaking|archive-date=13 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Becker|first=Claudia A.|date=2006|title=Review of Origins of Language: Constraints on Hypotheses|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4143902|journal=Rocky Mountain Review of Language and Literature|volume=60|issue=1|pages=147–149|doi=10.2307/4143902|jstor=4143902|issn=0361-1299|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2011, Johannson started making bots on Wikipedia, which have since made millions of edits.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hern |first=Alex |date=2014-08-05 |title=Wikipedia: meet the man who has edited 3m articles |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/aug/05/wikipedia-meet-the-man-who-has-edited-3m-articles |access-date=2025-12-16 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite news |last=Jervell |first=Ellen Emmerentze |date=July 13, 2014 |title=For This Author, 10,000 Wikipedia Articles Is a Good Day's Work |url=https://online.wsj.com/articles/for-this-author-10-000-wikipedia-articles-is-a-good-days-work-1405305001 |access-date=August 18, 2014 |work=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref>

In 2012, he presented the theory that [[Neanderthal language|Neanderthals used language]] in "Essay on Neanderthal Language".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Johansson |first=Sverker |date=2012 |title=The case for Neanderthal language – How strong is it? |url=https://urn.kb.se/resolve?urn=urn:nbn:se:du-13684 |journal=The Evolution of Language |publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company, Incorporated |pages=173–180}}</ref>

In 2014, a new article creation project was launched using Lsjbot, with the aim of producing basic articles about the world's geographical locations. As a result of this and subsequent projects, the bot created approximately 2.7 million articles in the same year, eventually reaching 9.5 million by 2019.<ref name="vice2020">{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=Kyle |title=The World's Second Largest Wikipedia Is Written Almost Entirely by One Bot |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/4agx8q/the-worlds-second-largest-wikipedia-is-written-almost-entirely-by-one-bot |website=Vice |date=11 February 2020 |access-date=16 September 2026}}</ref> This massive automated output was primarily distributed across the [[Swedish Wikipedia]], [[Cebuano Wikipedia]], and [[Waray Wikipedia]].<ref name="wsj2014">{{cite news |last1=Jervell |first1=Ellen Emmerentze |title=For This Author, 10,000 Wikipedia Articles Is a Good Day's Work |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/for-this-author-10-000-wikipedia-articles-is-a-good-days-work-1405305176 |newspaper=The Wall Street Journal |date=13 July 2014 |access-date=16 September 2026}}</ref> 

Although Lsjbot's mass-creation phase ceased in 2020 due to shifting community consensus, the bot's verifiable impact heavily dictates the size of these encyclopedias today. Lsjbot is responsible for initially creating nearly all of the Cebuano Wikipedia's {{NUMBEROF|articles|ceb|N}} articles and the vast majority of the Waray Wikipedia's {{NUMBEROF|articles|war|N}} articles. However, because the Swedish Wikipedia community later voted to mass-delete millions of the bot's automated stubs, only a fraction of Johansson's original contributions remain within the Swedish Wikipedia's current total of {{NUMBEROF|articles|sv|N}} articles.<ref name="popularscience2014">{{cite web |last1=Main |first1=Douglas |title=This Bot Has Written More Wikipedia Articles Than Anybody |url=https://www.popsci.com/article/science/bot-has-written-more-wikipedia-articles-anybody/ |website=Popular Science |date=14 July 2014 |access-date=16 September 2026}}</ref>
